data.one_liner: A Flutter wrapper for ListView that snaps to items at the end of user-scroll.
data.what_it_does: It wraps a ListView.builder to provide a snap-to-item behavior at the end of scrolling. It supports both horizontal and vertical scrolling directions, dynamic item sizing, opacity scaling, and custom positioning anchors.
use_when: You need a horizontal or vertical list that snaps to items like a carousel or picker.
You want unrestricted scrolling combined with snapping without using rigid page views.
You need to trigger callbacks when specific items gain focus during a scroll.
avoid_when: You require precise page-by-page snapping like a standard PageView with strict one-item bounds.
You are building complex custom physics-based scroll engines from scratch.
strengths: Supports both horizontal and vertical lists with unrestricted scroll behavior.
Provides dynamic item size and dynamic opacity scaling features.
Works out of the box with standard ListView builders and no external dependencies.
weaknesses: Requires providing a correct itemSize for proper calculation and snapping.
Tap detection on child items may conflict if items implement their own custom tap detectors, requiring manual key invocation.

alternatives.name: carousel_slider
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick carousel_slider if you specifically need a card carousel with auto-play and pagination indicators rather than a general snap-to-item list wrapper.

data.minimal_example:
Expanded(
  child: ScrollSnapList(
    onItemFocus: _onItemFocus,
    itemSize: 35,
    itemBuilder: _buildListItem,
    itemCount: data.length,
    reverse: true,
  ),
)
